text:
Priya N: Heads up — saw a weird dip in renewal-risk flags this morning. Looks like a chunk of mid-market accounts jumped to 'low-risk' overnight.
Ethan C: I noticed that too. Correlated with nightly dedupe job: merge-accounts-v3 ran at 02:12 UTC.
Priya N: Ugh. Those accounts had engagement_count > 0 before merge; post-merge engagement doubled for many. Healthscore calc grabbed the merged counter directly.
Jules T: merge-bot log says it aggregated contact rows by summing engagement_count. We should've kept canonical counts (max) or recomputed from events.
merge-bot: job "merge-accounts-v3" completed 2025-08-14T02:12:06Z 1,324 merges applied. Details: s3://playbooks/logs/merge-accounts-v3/2025-08-14.json
Ethan C: Impact: healthscore = base + log(engagement_count+1) so doubling engagement inflates score by ~0.3-0.6 pts -> flips some renewal buckets.
Priya N: We need a mitigation plan: 1) stop auto-merge in prod, 2) backfill corrected healthscores, 3) harden playbook to recompute healthscore from event_ledger instead of merged counters.
Jules T: Agreed. Quick detection query to enumerate suspects:
```
SELECT a.id, a.company, pre.engagement_count AS before, post.engagement_count AS after
FROM account_merge_audit am
JOIN accounts_pre_merge pre ON pre.id = am.source_id
JOIN accounts post ON post.id = am.dest_id
WHERE post.updated_at > now() - interval '24 hours' AND post.engagement_count > pre.engagement_count * 1.5;
```
Ethan C: For backfill we should recompute per-account from events to avoid repeating the merge bug. SQL snippet I tested in stage:
```
WITH agg AS (
  SELECT account_id, SUM(play_event = 'engaged') AS engagements
  FROM account_events
  WHERE occurred_at > now() - interval '3 years'
  GROUP BY account_id
)
UPDATE accounts a
SET engagement_count = agg.engagements,
    healthscore = compute_healthscore(a.base_score, agg.engagements)
FROM agg
WHERE a.id = agg.account_id;
```
Priya N: Nice. Also need metrics and safety: emit cs.dedupe.affected, cs.health.backfill.count, and add a safety-latch to abort backfill if >2% variance in median health per cohort.
Jules T: I'll open a PR to change merge-accounts-v3 to be idempotent and to compute aggregates from the event_ledger. Also add unit tests that simulate duplicate merges.
Ethan C: Can we do a sandbox run of the backfill first? ops-bot schedule please.
ops-bot: scheduled job 'sandbox-health-backfill-1758205432' for 2025-08-14T11:00Z.
Priya N: Also drafting a short CS note for owners so they don't get confused if their renewal scoring changes during remediations. I'll coordinate timing after the sandbox run.
merge-bot: rollback hook available. To disable auto-merge set env MERGE_AUTO=false and redeploy.
Jules T: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/playbooks/pull/512 (idempotent merges + ledger-based healthscore). Added telemetry and safety thresholds.
Ethan C: Sandbox run done: 1,120 accounts recomputed, median health delta -0.12, no unexpected nulls.
Priya N: Great. Plan: disable auto-merge now, run prod backfill in canary groups (1%, 10%, 100%) over 12h, monitor cs.health.backfill.count and renewal alerts. If variance >2% abort and notify ops.
Jules T: Deployed merge fix to canary. Ops to run prod backfill after canary validation window.
ops-bot: queued job 'prod-health-backfill-canary-1758205432' at 2025-08-14T15:00Z.
Priya N: Thanks all. After this I want a short playbook entry with rollback steps and a note in CS ops repo about how dedupe can affect computed signals. :memo:
